guide: Open Start here and type your names, your wedding day, your final headcount and your table count. Replace demo data: clear the sample rows and type your own.
List each DIY project in DIY projects with its hours, the cost to buy it and who owns it; add its supplies in Supplies with the quantity per guest, per table or once.
Open DIY Make or Buy to see Make, Buy or Make half for each project, then DIY Start Date and DIY Hours Load to plan the work before the wedding.
Use DIY Shopping Run and the Shopping list before each trip to the shop; quantities follow your headcount and tables.
Add every attire item in Attire shopping with its order-by date; Attire Order Planner names the next item to order.
Log each gift in the Gift Log the day it arrives, with the cash amount for cash gifts and where the money goes.
Write each note in Thank-you notes; the Thank-you backlog lists the gifts still without one, oldest first, and Thank-you Pace says how many a week finish them.
Cash Gifts and Funding and the Honeymoon Gap show what cash gifts do for the budget and the honeymoon; expected gifts are never counted until received.
Enter the fee your payment provider charges in your settings and mark the gifts that came through it; Payment Service Fee shows what you keep.
After the wedding open Final Budget Check and Cost per Guest Check, then Vendor Balance Check, Returns and Refunds Tracker and Paperwork Tracker.
Wrap-up Readiness counts what is still open and says Close the wedding when nothing is left.
Use the 18 tools, print 12 sheets and 12 pages, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
A couple with a small wedding uses the gift log, the thank-you notes, the final budget and the wrap-up with no DIY: leave the DIY and attire sheets empty.
No macros; it works in Excel and Google Sheets and prints for the day. Why a workbook: one flat price, no vendor ever sees your details, no gift fees and your own numbers.
What this is not: not a booking service, not a payment service, and not legal or tax advice. Check with your officiant or local office, and ask your accountant what your own rules need.

listing.title: Wedding After and Gifts Excel Template: DIY Make or Buy, Thank-you Note Tracker, Cash Gifts, Final Budget, Cost per Guest, Returns
listing.headline: Make or buy, thank every guest and close the wedding budget in one workbook
listing.description:
Close the last part of your wedding in one Excel workbook. Built for an engaged couple who make some of the decor themselves, log every shower and engagement gift, write thank-you notes and want to know what the wedding really cost. DIY projects and Supplies work out the quantity from your headcount and table count, set the cost to make against the cost to buy and say Make, Buy or Make half. The DIY start date, the DIY hours load and the shopping list keep the work done before the wedding. Attire shopping lists outfits, shoes, accessories and alterations with an order-by date.

The Gift Log, Thank-you notes and Thank-you backlog show every gift without a note, oldest first, against your own alert days, and the pace tool says how many notes a week finish the job. Cash gifts are logged separately, linked to the honeymoon fund and the budget gap, and expected gifts are never counted until they are received. You enter the fee your payment provider charges and see what you keep.

After the day, Final Budget against Actual shows planned, committed, paid and still due for every category, the cost per guest against your own target, the vendor balances still due, rentals to return and deposits to claim, and a paperwork and name change list in generic words with optional rows you can edit. A wrap-up check tells you when the wedding can be closed.

18 tools answer weekly questions with a clear verdict. Print 12 sheets and 12 pages, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to guests, helpers, family and vendors. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Guests appear as names only. It is a planning kit, not a booking or payment service, and gives no legal or tax advice. This is part eight of the Wedding Planning suite.
